name: User-Agent Parser
description: Parse browser, engine, OS, device and crawler from User-Agent strings offline with the matching rule shown; summarize UAs in access logs
help: The rule set ships inside the plugin and works fully offline. Every result shows the matching rule id and the matched part of the UA; hover to see the raw pattern.

Rules are tried in order and the first match wins: in-app and Chromium-based browsers come before Chrome and Safari. Crawler rules cover major search engines, link previews, AI crawlers, SEO and monitoring services, headless browsers and common command-line and HTTP clients; clients named with bot / crawler / spider fall back to a generic crawler.

A UA can be spoofed freely, so results only describe what the string claims. Chromium-based browsers freeze the platform version (Windows always 10.0, macOS always 10.15.7, Android model K); results point this out.

Batch mode accepts one UA per line, a CSV column (defaults to a column named User-Agent) or combined-format access logs (third quoted field). Identical UAs are merged and counted, with device, browser, OS and crawler distributions, exportable as CSV / JSON.

single.title: User-Agent
single.hint: Or click “This app” to parse the UA of the app's built-in browser

notes.frozenPlatform: Chromium-based browsers freeze the platform version in the UA, so the OS version here may not be real (Client Hints are needed for that).
notes.windows11: Windows 10 and Windows 11 both report Windows NT 10.0 and cannot be told apart.
notes.reducedModel: The reduced Android UA fixes the device model to K, so the real model is unknown.
notes.macMayBeIpad: iPads browse in desktop mode by default with the same UA as Safari on a Mac, so this may also be an iPad.
